title: Inference KPI staleness detector and OTLP rescue runner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: several tenants and model variants intermittently stop producing expected inference KPIs (per-request latency, token counts, error categories) for extended intervals. Current alerting trips only when raw Prometheus scrape fails, which misses partial ingest gaps caused by intermediate OTLP gateways, transient schema rejections, or tenant-side batching delays. This ticket implements a light-weight staleness detection layer and an "OTLP rescue runner" to automatically rehydrate missing KPI windows from durable buffers or DLQs.
design_summary: 1) Staleness scoring: compute a rolling per-tenant/per-model 'staleness score' derived from expected cadence (heartbeat histograms), last-seen metric timestamps, and variance of token-rate. 2) Staleness policies: configurable thresholds for warning/critical that map to actions (alert, telemetry annotation, rescue). 3) OTLP Rescue Runner: a controlled worker that attempts incremental replays from the OTLP dead-letter store or backup S3/BigQuery slices, performs lightweight dedupe, and re-inserts harmonized metrics into the ingest pipeline with provenance tags (rescue=true). 4) Observability: dashboard tiles with staleness heatmap, rescue outcomes, and per-run reconciliation statistics. 5) Safety: rate-limit rescue replays to avoid double-write storms and ensure idempotency via deterministic envelope IDs.
success_criteria:
- Detect >95% of partial KPI outages (gaps >60s) in staging within a week.
- Rescue runner successfully rehydrates >=90% of recoverable windows in test runs without causing ingestion backpressure.
- New dashboards show staleness trends and per-tenant rescue counts.
- Alerts for critical staleness in prod with actionable runbook steps.
constraints:
- Must not increase tail latency on primary ingestion path.
- Rescue writes must be traceable and clearly flagged to downstream consumers and billing.
- Avoid schema drift: rescued envelopes must be normalized to current proto schema before reingest.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Observability and Serving teams. Agreed to prototype scoring rules in staging. (Meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/KPI+Staleness+Kickoff).
2026-02-18: Prototype implemented as a sidecar process reading from the metrics ingestion Kafka topic; scoring rule v1 available in staging. Demo recorded and shared with PM.

2026-02-22: Initial synthetic test: injected 10 gap windows across 5 tenants; staleness detector flagged 9/10; false positive caused by irregular client batching — adjusted heartbeat baseline heuristic.

2026-02-27: Implemented OTLP Rescue Runner MVP that replays from DLQ (S3 prefix) and writes back through the ingest gateway with header X-Rescue-Run:ENG-902345. Created deterministic dedupe key using request id + timestamp bucket.
2026-03-02: Integration test against staging ingestion showed rescue throughput 80r/s with CPU stable on worker fleet. Added protective backoff to prevent overloading the gateway. PR opened.
2026-03-04: Design review feedback from infra: need metric-level provenance field and opt-in per-tenant rescue. Added config knobs and tenant opt-out list.

2026-03-05: Security review checklist prepped; DPO asked for explicit retention TTL for rescue provenance metadata (added to runbook). Next: load-test replays to validate no impact to Prometheus scrape exporter and finalize runbook.
next_steps: Finalize idempotency contract for rescue writes and add deterministic envelope generator to the runner.
Run 72-hour continuous replay load test in staging and capture ingest latency histograms.
Wire new dashboard panels into Console per-route metrics and add canary alerting for early detection.
Ship limited opt-in to five enterprise tenants for validation before wider rollout.
